_HOW_TO_USE: 2. Fill every {{PLACEHOLDER}} and each block's content. Delete blocks/tabs you don't need.
3. Tag each field/block audience:'internal' (default, war-room only) or 'both' (safe to share).
6. Wire the subdomain in next.config.ts + vercel domains add; gate internal with a NON-guessable pw.
_METHOD: Six tabs = six disciplines in sequence. PRE-CALL: orient before contact (True North, register/intent, intel, questions, landmines). EX-ANTE: file a decision receipt BEFORE the event (hypothesis + predicted Y-gate + pre-committed move + falsifier) so you can be scored later. FORGE: pressure-test the brief's own claims against external substrates via an independent skeptic (grounded / inference / struck). RECOIL: after the event, close the receipt — belief-update ledger (confidence x conviction), kairos/quiet-signals, risk flags, next steps. WAR GAME: adversarial + kinematic — measured manifold, BAR/LAB/COURT gauntlet, ATG pre-mortem on the critical path vs their real objections. DEFENSIBILITY: translate the method into the counterpart's native register (Rosetta) + a 5-verb x 4-proofing matrix + the antifragile-core / lossless-translation test.

blocks.intro: Lyndon Oh, co-founder and CTO of VICO, an AI forecasting company for political, geopolitical and economic event risk. Everything about his view of Zach is second-hand through Joe; the company facts are public.

items.html: He read the deck, and liked it. Joe (2026-10-02): "We obviously reviewed your profile and pulled up kind of the pitch deck and went through it... he has spent a decent amount of time in that." Zach's event tracking showed the same.
What he responded to (Joe's relay): "build capability. Prototype capability. IQ leadership." And: "Zach could solve some of our current problems." Joe does not know which problems.

His open question is the seat. Joe relaying Lyndon: "we don't know where Zach would fit within our organization... should it be a PE role? Should it be the VP of engineering?" Joe: "He is currently thinking single-threaded." Joe says he will coach him toward a broader conversation; that may or may not happen before the call.

Comp frame, second-hand. Joe (2026-09-30): Lyndon "is viewing this as a little bit closer to $300,000, $300,000 being that VP of engineering. He's hesitant... to have that conversation" because of Oxenham's fee, which Joe plans to cap. Joe had floated "mid-$200s" with equity.

Company stage. VICO was founded in 2025 by Anthony Vinci and Lyndon Oh; public reporting shows an undisclosed pre-seed round. Platform launched 2026-02-03; forecasts on the Bloomberg Terminal; indexes on US hard power, tokenization and deglobalization. Joe (2026-10-02, unverified): "they work with the DOD. Apparently they have a couple customers in there." A ~$300K VP seat at pre-seed is possible but unusual: verify runway before trusting the frame.

Lyndon's background (LinkedIn and data-broker profiles, grade B/C): PhD Economics (University of St. Gallen), MSc International Relations (LSE); before VICO, co-founder and CEO of Ozone, CEO of Findyr, founder and CEO of Leviathan Analytics; prior time at Google and Facebook. That matches Joe's 2026-09-14 claim of Meta then Google, previously unverified. Read: a founder-CEO and economist now carrying the CTO title, so build and prototype capacity is plausibly the gap he feels.
Anthony Vinci, CEO: first CTO of the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; senior roles at Bridgewater and Cerberus. The next call after Lyndon, per Joe.

Org shape (2026-09-17 call): flat org, the Product Engineer seat reports to Lyndon, and a VP of Engineering role is also open that would sit above it. A Solution Architect role is open too (2026-09-30).
Competition. Joe is submitting other candidates. Joe (2026-09-30): "Nick's a young gun out of DC." Lyndon himself first asked Joe about a "young gun" (2026-09-17 record).
Office. Joe (2026-10-02): "Lyndon and Anthony are in New York... I think that's their main one. DC is their secondary." "You don't have to travel to DC." NYC address still owed by Joe.

Comp floor already given (correction, 2026-10-04 verbatim re-read). Joe asked on 09-30 whether Zach would take "somewhere in the mid-$200s" with equity; Zach: "Yeah, or even like less depending on what the cap table looks like." Joe therefore holds a number below the ~$300K Lyndon reportedly floated. Assume it may reach Lyndon.
Competition. Joe (09-30) is also submitting Nick, "a young gun out of DC", and always sends multiple profiles. The fight is not just the seat, it is senior-scope vs a cheaper Product Engineer.

Funding conflict (unresolved). This SSOT's 10-03 read is an undisclosed pre-seed; a Tracxn search snippet (2026-10-04) claims $103M over 3 rounds for "Vico", likely a name collision with another Vico. Do not rely on either; ask runway directly.

Pace signal (2026-10-09): Joe said on 2026-10-04 he would reach Lyndon "early tomorrow morning" to set timing; the invite arrived 2026-10-09. A next-day promise became five days. Read: either Lyndon is busy or the seat is not urgent for him. Not a red flag alone.

Still owed by Joe: the NYC office address and the "alignment signals to emphasize" he offered after the 2026-10-02 debrief. Neither has arrived. Ask Joe for the signals by Tue 10-13 if useful; do not wait on them.
Parallel loop: monday.com FDE assignment session is Thu 2026-10-15, the day after this call. Keep both honest; do not use one as leverage on the other at req_reality 2.

blocks._doc: QUESTIONS + LANDMINES: what to ask, what a good answer sounds like, what not to do.
blocks.intro: Ask before pitching. The first ten minutes should be his problems, not my deck: he has already read the deck.

items.html: Open with his words: "Joe said you think I could help with some current problems. Which ones are on fire right now?" · look for: two or three named, specific problems (a system, a customer, a deadline), not "scaling" in the abstract

The seat probe (req_reality gate question): "Does this land in an existing function, or is it something you're still designing?" · look for: an answer in his own words. Bespoke-and-still-being-designed is the Fanatics/HypeLab shape: keep the next step to a written read on one problem, not a role negotiation

Where does revenue come from in the next 12 months? Bloomberg and private-market clients, or government pilots? · look for: one motion he is betting on, with a reason. Public sector cycles run long; the private side is the faster proof
Who builds today? Engineering headcount, who ships the forecasts, how the open VP of Engineering role relates to this one · look for: a real number and a clear reporting line

His CTO question, from the deck: how far down can a doubting analyst open the path from sources to a single forecast number? And how does the system notice its own calibration drifting after a shock? · look for: whether he lights up (this is his domain) or deflects
Runway, asked plainly: "What does the next 12 to 18 months look like on funding?" · look for: a straight answer. A pre-seed company with a $300K seat needs a reason
Close: offer to come back within a few days with a short written read on one of his named problems; confirm the Anthony call · look for: he names the problem to write about

Landmine: comp. Do not raise it. Joe owns the fee and the number. If Lyndon raises it: flexible, people and problem first, Joe has the range. Zach (2026-09-30): "I'm not going to negotiate against myself." If he cites a number Joe gave him: do not confirm or restate it. "I'd rather we figure out what the seat is first; Joe and I can sort the number after."

Landmine: pitching ARCS as a product. He builds explainable AI forecasting; ARCS reads as a neighboring product. Use it only as proof of how I work (source-graded, receipts, backtest-style scoring), never as a thing I want to bring with me
Landmine: the Solution Architect hat. Do not agree to forward-deployed, DC-heavy travel by default. Zach's limit (2026-09-30): not "traveling 25 to 50% of the time"
Landmine: clearances. Do not overclaim government access. Ask what the DOD work requires instead
Landmine: seniority. Do not argue with the young-gun framing. Frame senior as de-risking, the line Zach already gave Joe: "you're not paying somebody to learn on your dime"

fields.label: Hypothesis / expecting to see
fields.value: Lyndon names at least two specific current problems in the first half of the call, and at least one sits outside pure front-end engineering (data pipeline, prototype velocity, go-to-market or positioning). He is open to scoping a role around those problems rather than the Product Engineer JD as written.

fields.label: Predicted Y-gate
fields.value: YELLOW · principal interest is real, but the seat and the comp frame are both unverified until he states them himself

fields.label: Pre-committed move
fields.value: Ask for the problems first and listen. If he names them: offer a short written read on one within a few days, and ask for the Anthony call. Ask about runway plainly. Never raise comp. If he only describes the fixed JD: ask once whether the problems he mentioned to Joe live inside that JD; if not, say so and let Joe carry the reframe.

fields.label: Belief most likely to update
fields.value: Whether the ~$300K VP-level frame is Lyndon's own at a 2025 pre-seed company, or Joe's packaging of a Product Engineer budget.

fields.label: Falsifier
fields.value: If Lyndon cannot name one concrete current problem, or treats the call as a screen for the front-end JD with no interest in scope, the 'solve our current problems' relay was recruiter amplification: downgrade to FORK, treat the role as Product Engineer only, and weigh it against the other live threads on that basis.
